title: Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa Disputes Casso Claim That Opponents of Pay Raise Are Collecting It
excerpt: District 3 Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa says she and two fellow council members never accepted the council pay raise approved in October 2024, pushing back on former mayoral candidate Alfonso “Poncho” Casso’s claim that all council members are receiving the extra pay.
content:
District 3 Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa has publicly pushed back on former mayoral candidate Alfonso “Poncho” Casso’s claim that council members who opposed a controversial salary increase are still receiving the additional pay.

Cigarroa responded in the comment section of a report about Casso’s appearance on Beyond the Headlines, where Casso said he has open records showing that all council members — including mayoral candidate Alyssa Cigarroa — received the higher salary despite publicly opposing the increase.

Cigarroa wrote that she, Alyssa Cigarroa and Councilman Tyler King did not accept the salary increase the City Council voted to approve in October 2024. She pointed to Section 2.02 of the Laredo City Charter, saying council-approved salary increases ordinarily cannot take effect until an elected official’s next term when the ordinance is adopted at least three months beforehand. She said the 2024 increase was instead approved as an “administrative adjustment,” which allowed participating council members to receive the additional pay right away.

“To this day, we three do not receive the additional $1,650.00 per month in our paychecks,” she wrote.

The two accounts directly conflict. Casso maintains that open records support his claim; Cigarroa maintains that the three council members who opposed the increase never took the extra monthly pay. The dispute turns on what the city’s payroll records actually show, and Webb Watch 956 has not independently verified those records.

Melissa Cigarroa is related to mayoral candidate Alyssa Cigarroa.
